subject: Quantify pilot — performance cadence and fallback options
messages:
From: Claire Ng <claire@quantify.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Keller <tk@quantify.ai>
Date: 2026-12-08T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quantify pilot — SLO targets and token profiles (follow-up)

Jonas / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — this was helpful. I wanted to capture the performance goals and a few constraints from our side so you have a single place to react. The two main features we care about are interactive analytics chat (users type large queries against docs) and scheduled batch summarization. High level:

- Interactive chat (primary): typical session has ~6k tokens of context (multi-document), expect up to 2k tokens generated per response (streaming required). Target: end-to-end p95 latency <= 400 ms for the first partial token to arrive; p95 end-to-end completion for full outputs is less strict (<= 2.5s) but lower is better.
- Batch summarization (secondary): throughput requirement of ~10k documents/hour; latency is not critical but throughput and cost matter.

Specific asks / constraints:
- We need a fallback plan for requests that exceed the 6k context (we will have occasional long sessions up to ~12k input tokens). Ideally the system should degrade gracefully rather than fail.
- Concurrency: expected peak concurrent interactive users ~120, average 40.
- Budget: initial pilot monthly token budget ~6M tokens.

Attached is a quick spreadsheet with sample session lengths and percentiles. Can you confirm which model variants and quantization profiles would meet the interactive P95 requirement for our expected context window? Also, what tradeoffs would you recommend between throughput and latency (e.g., batching thresholds, streaming vs full response)?

Appreciate a short runbook we can use for the pilot (what we'll test, metrics to capture, and canary schedule).

Thanks,
Claire
Head of Product 
Quantify AI

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Claire Ng <claire@quantify.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-08T17:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quantify pilot — SLO targets and token profiles (follow-up)

Claire — thanks for the clear summary and the spreadsheet. Quick confirmation on what we heard, then a proposed test plan and next steps below.

What we heard (confirmation):
- Interactive chat: typical input ~6k tokens; outputs up to 2k tokens; streaming required.
- Target: p95 partial-token arrival <= 400 ms; completion p95 <= 2.5s.
- Occasional long contexts up to ~12k tokens — need graceful fallback.
- Peak concurrency ~120.

Proposed pilot plan (high-level):
1) Baseline perf matrix: run microbenchmarks for three model profiles (open-13B quantized, open-70B q4/8, and a small low-cost 3B variant) across a set of context sizes (2k, 4k, 6k, 12k). We'll capture p50/p95/p99 partial-token arrival times and end-to-end completion.
2) Canary: mirror a subset of live sessions (500 unique sessions, up to 50 concurrent) for 48 hours. This will exercise real-query patterns and streaming behavior.
3) Fallback policy: plan to implement (a) prefix/KV caching for repeated docs, (b) streaming partials + model-fanout (first deliver from a fast low-context model, then synthesize full answer from a heavier model if needed), and (c) chunked retrieval + progressive summarization for >6k contexts.
4) Success criteria: for pilot, we aim for p95 partial arrival <= 400 ms for >= 90% of interactive sessions under the canary load.

Next steps I need from your side:
- Confirm which 48-hour window works for the canary next week.
- Approve access to a narrow telemetry slice (request ids + timestamps + token counts) so we can measure p95.

Laura / Rishi — added you for technical validation and to propose runtime knobs (batch size targets, kernel profiles, recommended hardware). I attached our draft perf profiles PDF — we'll iterate as you test.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, Claire Ng <claire@quantify.ai>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-09T09:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quantify pilot — SLO targets and token profiles (follow-up)

Jonas / Claire — looping in the short technical feasibility summary and recommended guardrails. High-level takeaways first, then numbers and proposed runbook.

TL;DR
- For interactive streaming with 6k input + up to 2k output: a 13B quantized (q4) profile on a modern GPU (A10/A100 class) can typically hit p95 partial-token arrival in the 200–350 ms range when concurrency is moderate (<= 50 concurrency per GPU node) and prefix/KV caching is effective.
- 70B variants give richer completions but increase single-request latency by ~2–3x at large contexts; use them for non-latency-critical completions or as a background post-process.
- For sessions that exceed 6k input tokens, recommend progressive degradation: (1) truncate least-recent content and apply a summarization pre-pass (2) or route to a chunked pipeline that stitches answers with progressive summarization and streaming partials. Both approaches preserve UX while bounding latency.

Numbers (empirical estimates from our internal bench):
- open-13B, q4: 2k context generation (streaming start): p50 ~ 70 ms, p95 ~ 220 ms; 6k context: p50 ~ 180 ms, p95 ~ 320 ms; 12k context: p50 ~ 420 ms, p95 ~ 1.1 s (not ideal for strict interactive SLO).
- open-70B, q4/8: 6k context: p95 ~ 900 ms; 12k: p95 > 2.5 s (recommended only if user accepts slower response or background post-process).
- small 3B variant: very fast for short contexts but declines rapidly with +6k context due to memory fetches; good as a fast-fallback for first-pass answers.

Runtime knobs and tradeoffs:
- Batching: increase batching improves GPU utilization and throughput but adds queueing latency. For interactive targets, cap batching window to <= 8 ms and prioritize low-latency scheduling.
- KV/prefix caching: huge wins for repeated doc lookups; cache hit can reduce p95 by 30–60% depending on reuse.
- Quantization: q4 reduces latency and memory footprint with minor quality impact; for mission-critical answers you can hybridize (fast q4 first, then re-score with higher-precision).
- Streaming strategy: emit partial tokens immediately from the fast model, and optionally fan-out a heavier model to generate a refined result streamed later (UX shows users value early partials).

Proposed pilot runbook (short):
1) Benchmarks: we will run controlled runs for the three model profiles across 2k/4k/6k/12k contexts (48 hours). Deliverable: latency matrix + token-per-second profiles.
2) Canary: 48-hour window with 500 sessions and up to 50 concurrency. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 partial and completion times, upstream request size distributions, and cache-hit rates.
3) Fallback deployment: enable an automatic route that (a) serves from 13B q4, (b) when context >6k triggers summarize-and-chunk pipeline and marks request as degraded in telemetry, (c) for extreme cases returns a short partial and a link to a background full result.
4) Monitoring: dashboard showing partial-token p95, completion p95, cache-hit ratio, model-fallback counts; set alerts if p95 partial > 700 ms or fallback ratio > 10% during canary.

Attachments: I included a short PDF with the microbenchmark graphs and a CSV we will use as the baseline for the canary. We'll upload the raw traces to the shared Drive for deeper analysis after each run.

Questions for you, Claire:
- Are you able to accept a progressive-degradation UX (short partials + background refined result) for sessions that exceed 6k tokens?
- Can you provide a sample of true session traces (anonymized) so the bench runs match real distributions?

Happy to run the first controlled bench tomorrow if you give us a green light on the anonymized traces and a canary window.

—Laura
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
